# seq

Print a numeric sequence through MoonX.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/seq 1 5

moonx cli/seq -s , 0 0.5 2

moonx cli/seq -w 8 12
```

Accept LAST, FIRST LAST or FIRST INCREMENT LAST. The default first value and increment are both one.

## Common options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s VALUE`, `--separator VALUE` | Replace the separator between values. |
| `-w`, `--equal-width` | Pad values to equal width. |
| `-f VALUE`, `--format VALUE` | Use one e/E/f/F/g/G/a/A conversion. |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

## Notes

- Floating-point behavior follows the fixed Linux amd64 extended-precision profile. Extreme textual precision, exponents and scales are bounded.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
